citation.title: Toward Large Language Model-Driven Symbolic Topology Optimisation for Rapid Structural Concept Generation in Manufacturable Design
citation.venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing 10(4), 117

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The LLM-generated cantilever design reaches about 87.5% of the stiffness of the classical SIMP result; the heat-sink design reaches about 94.3% of reference thermal performance.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: The abstract asserts reduced computational cost without a quantitative speed-up factor or matched runtime.
claim.alternatives: The abstract also claims less repeated finite-element simulation and reduced computational cost, but does not quantify the comparison.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP topology optimization (cantilever); reference thermal solution for heat sink
baseline.problem_size: Cantilever structural benchmark; heat-sink optimization; paper also presents thermofluid, compliant mechanism, and 3D examples (Sections 4.1–4.5)
baseline.classical_time: not stated for the classical comparison
baseline.ml_time: Thermofluid example: about 3–8 s per generation iteration, overall convergence within a few minutes (Section 4.4); no matched SIMP timing
baseline.quality_metric: stiffness for cantilever; thermal performance for heat sink
baseline.quality_gap: Cantilever result is approximately 12.5% below classical SIMP stiffness; heat-sink result reaches about 94.3% of reference thermal performance (Abstract).

R1.evidence: The primary comparison in the abstract is design quality (stiffness and thermal performance), with no speed comparison at matched quality or time.

R2.evidence: The abstract compares performance values but gives no classical runtime or solver comparison.

R3.evidence: The primary outcome is quality-only; no quantitative speed comparison is made.

R4.evidence: Sections 3.2 and 4 describe symbolic layouts evaluated with heuristic or surrogate indicators; the 3D structural response is explicitly approximated through geometric/connectivity indicators, not FE analysis of returned designs.

reporting.n_test_cases: Five example groups: cantilever, heat sink, thermofluid channel, compliant mechanism, and 3D topology (Sections 4.1–4.5)

notes: The paper includes thermofluid examples, but the coded primary comparison is the in-scope structural cantilever benchmark.
